I would like to propose the idea of a "changelog", illustrated here:

https://i.imgur.com/BJAQ0AW.jpg

Additionally, I think this feature should be optional (but on by default) for each subverse. This is to give the creators of subverses maximum flexibility and freedom to run things the way they see fit.

If this is implement alongside the other idea that I proposed (of competing subverses,) then users themselves can decide whether they want to trust a subverse with the changelog disabled or not. Some people may like the idea of extreme transparency, others may not.

If it is enabled:

Then users will now be able to tell who posted a deleted comment, who deleted it, at what date and time, etc. should they feel the need to investigate. I think having such an ability will allow users to feel better about their user experience and enable better trust amongst moderators and users.

For the changelog itself, I am imagining it as something of a database. Perhaps with two main sections, one for submissions, one for comments. Each deletion is given an entry number that can be used to reference it should it come up in discussion. Moderators who make a deletion can be given the choice of specifying why they deleted something, but in practice, they may not if it is very obviously spam or something undesirable.
